title: Sell Mineral Rights in New Town, ND
primaryKeyword: sell mineral rights new town nd
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in New Town, ND
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near New Town, ND on the Fort Berthold Reservation? We explain trust vs. fee minerals and give you a straight offer either way.
heroLead: New Town sits at the center of the Fort Berthold Reservation, and mineral ownership here splits into two very different categories that a lot of owners don't realize matter until they try to sell.
intro: If your interest is trust land owned by an MHA Nation allottee, it's administered by the Bureau of Indian Affairs and any sale requires federal approval, a longer process than a standard deed. If it's fee minerals within or near the reservation boundary, it transfers through the Mountrail County Recorder like any other North Dakota interest. We tell owners honestly which category applies to them before anything else happens.

sections.heading: Trust minerals and the BIA approval process
paragraphs: Trust interests near New Town can't be sold with a simple mineral deed. The Bureau of Indian Affairs has to approve the transfer, which involves additional paperwork and a longer timeline than fee mineral sales elsewhere in the county. We walk owners through exactly what that process looks like rather than promise a fast close that isn't realistic.

sections.heading: Fee minerals near the reservation boundary
paragraphs: Not every New Town-area interest is trust land. Fee minerals here transfer through a standard recorded deed, and this part of Mountrail County has seen strong Bakken and Sanish field development, so a fee interest near New Town can be genuinely valuable. We check the state well index for your specific tract either way.

sections.heading: The Four Bears Bridge area and nearby development
paragraphs: The Missouri River and Lake Sakakawea shape a lot of how drilling has unfolded around New Town, with the Four Bears Bridge connecting communities across the water and development following the accessible ground on both sides. Some tracts near the water have seen less drilling simply due to access, which is part of what we check before pricing an interest.
Whether your family's mineral rights are trust or fee, we start every conversation the same way, by confirming exactly what you own and what's actually producing before talking about a number.

faqs.question: How do I know if my New Town-area interest is trust or fee minerals?
faqs.answer: Send us your Division Order, deed, or any BIA correspondence you have and we can usually tell within a day which category applies to you.

faqs.question: How long does a trust mineral sale actually take?
faqs.answer: Longer than a fee mineral sale, since it requires Bureau of Indian Affairs approval. We'll give you a realistic timeline once we know your specific situation rather than a vague promise.

faqs.question: Is New Town-area acreage in a strong part of the Bakken?
faqs.answer: Yes, this part of Mountrail County sits near the productive Sanish field, so both trust and fee interests here are often worth a serious look.

faqs.question: Does being near Lake Sakakawea affect whether our minerals have been drilled?
faqs.answer: It can, since access along the river and lake shapes where operators have been able to place wells. We check activity near your specific tract rather than assume based on the general area.
